title: Blackbox regression triage - quant pilot
summary: Weekly POC sync to triage an unexpected quality regression seen on INT8 runs. Reviewed perf deltas across INT8/FP8, looked at outlier prompts, discussed KV/prefix caching behavior and rollout gating. Agreed to run targeted blacklist of 120 prompts, share detailed CSVs, and run a repeat on a fresh GB16 instance with a survival fallback to FP16 when delta > threshold.
next_steps: Redwood to send CSV of per-prompt delta and token-level timing by EOD 2026-08-22
SignalCraft to provide the 120 blacklisted prompts and mark golden set by 2026-08-24
Run rerun on fresh GB16 instance (Redwood) and post results to shared sheet by 2026-08-26
Schedule a 30m regression readout with engineering (week of 2026-08-31)
Document fallback policy (FP16 auto-fallback threshold) and add to rollout playbook
action_items: Liam O'Connor: produce per-prompt CSV + latency histogram (due: 2026-08-22)
Sofia Patel: run KV-cache disabled run and share logs (due: 2026-08-24)
Tom Wu: export SignalCraft blacklisted prompts and golden set labels (due: 2026-08-24)
Evan Brooks: run systematic QA pass on top 50 regressions and attach examples (due: 2026-08-25)
Devon Ruiz: provision GB16 repeat cluster and hand over access creds (due: 2026-08-23)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Devon Ruiz (Redwood), Anika Rao (SignalCraft), Tom Wu (SignalCraft), Priya Menon (SignalCraft), Evan Brooks (SignalCraft QA)

Summary note: quick sync after customer reported a spike in generation quality regressions on INT8 variants over the last 48h. We'll go through top-line numbers then look at prompt-level anomalies.

00:00:08 Liam (Redwood AE): okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining um today we're going to focus on the regression triage we saw on the int8 runs, uh just to set expectation 45 minutes of triage and then 10 minutes of next steps.

00:00:24 Anika (SignalCraft): thanks Liam, yep we pulled a few failing examples overnight, pretty concerned because customer-facing throughput was fine but some generative outputs degraded for product search summarization.

00:00:38 Sofia (Redwood SE): quick clarifying q — when you say degraded are you seeing hallucinations or missing entities?

00:00:43 Anika: mostly entity drop and occasional hallucinated dates, like the model invents a timeline, weirdly it was only on INT8 we've been running FP8 side-by-side and FP8 looks fine.

00:00:58 Liam: right, so our perf dashboard shows token-level latency dropped as expected on int8, cost down ~38%, but quality delta for some prompts jumped beyond your threshold (0.12 on nll-based metric).

00:01:14 Tom: interesting, the failure cluster correlates with long prefix prompts that include a codeblock + metadata header, we saw more regressions when the prefix is longer than 700 tokens.

00:01:29 Sofia: that could tie into KV-cache and attention kernel switching at longer sequences — sometimes our kernel selection heuristics pick a different attention path for int8 that isn't numerically identical.

00:01:42 Priya: can that cause entity drops?

00:01:44 Sofia: yeah if kv alignment or quant rounding introduces small drift it can cascade across long context windows and cause the final token distribution to shift.

00:02:00 Evan (QA): we logged 76 unique prompt ids with >0.2 quality delta, top 20 represent 68% of user-visible regressions. I'll share the ids.

00:02:12 Liam: perfect, can you walk us through one or two examples?

00:02:18 Evan: sure, example prompt id sc-1124 — long metadata header, then a bullet list of items to summarize, FP8 output preserves three entities; INT8 drops the second entity and substitutes a generic pronoun leading to failure in downstream extraction.

00:02:36 Sofia: mm-hmm ok and what about temperature / sampling differences? were both runs deterministic?

00:02:40 Tom: yes both deterministic, seed fixed, same model revision pinned, only quantization variant changed (FP8 vs INT8).

00:02:50 Liam: did you run with prefix cache enabled?

00:02:53 Tom: yes by default cache on, because we see throughput benefits in prod.

00:02:57 Sofia: can we try a cache-disabled run to see if kv write/read is implicated. There are cases where cached kv uses a slightly different layout which can amplify quantization error.

00:03:10 Devon (Redwood): I'll provision a cache-disabled run on our repro cluster, that should take ~6 hours to complete for the 120 prompts, but we'll prioritize the top 20.

00:03:22 Anika: top 20 first would be great. Also, we noticed regressions cluster by prompt type: code-heavy vs legalese vs conversational. Code-heavy seems most sensitive.

00:03:36 Sofia: not surprising — structured tokens and code tokens often have different embedding distributions which quantizers handle differently.

00:03:47 Liam: quick question — are these requests mainly hitting our GB16 instances or mixed GPU types?

00:03:52 Tom: in prod they autoroute, but for the poc we've pinned to GB16, the repro runs were on an older GB16 image that had an older kernel, I think that might matter.

00:04:07 Sofia: ah kernel and CUDA runtime versions can subtly change fp32->int8 codepaths, that could be a confounder. Devon can you verify the kernel / cudnn versions?

00:04:17 Devon: yes I'll capture the exact image hash and runtime. We'll also re-run on freshly provisioned GB16 with our recommended runtime.

00:04:26 Anika: would a fallback to FP16 be an acceptable interim safety mechanism if we detect a prompt with > threshold delta?

00:04:34 Priya: yes we prefer product correctness over perf for now, fallback is fine as long as it's deterministic and we have the logs.

00:04:42 Liam: ok fallback policy seems reasonable: if per-prompt quality delta > 0.15 on the evaluation metric and persists across two runs, trigger FP16 fallback. We'll add that to the rollout gating.

00:04:57 Evan: one more datapoint — latency improvement on INT8 vs FP8 for these prompts is variable: some get 40% token speedup others only 8%. Not uniformly better.

00:05:09 Sofia: that variability matches kernel switching and sequence-length effects; shorter sequences sometimes don't benefit as much.

00:05:20 Tom: we also saw memory layout differences when quantizing certain attention layers which affected transient working set and might produce different softmax numerics.

00:05:33 Liam: I want to make sure we separate 3 axes: model runtime/kernel, quantization algorithm (symmetric vs asymmetric scale), and caching. Let's set experiments that isolate each.

00:05:45 Anika: Agreed. What do you propose as the isolation matrix?

00:05:50 Sofia: matrix: (1) same runtime image, cache enabled, quant variant (int8 vs fp8), (2) same runtime image, cache disabled, quant variant, (3) different runtime image (fresh), cache enabled, quant variant. That will let us see canonically where delta arises.

00:06:10 Liam: timeline?

00:06:12 Devon: I can spin the jobs today, prioritize the top 20 prompts first and run matrix set 1 & 2 in parallel. Should finish within 6-8 hours for top20, full 120 set overnight.

00:06:25 Priya: Great. On the metric front — are we using token-level log-prob delta or downstream extraction F1?

00:06:32 Evan: both. We have token-nll deltas for bulk triage and then we run the downstream extractor test to measure user-visible regression. F1 drop > 0.05 flags an alert.

00:06:44 Liam: excellent, align metrics and thresholds in the shared sheet please.

00:06:52 Anika: another question — can Redwood provide the per-layer quant scales so we can inspect which layers have the largest scale variance?

00:07:01 Sofia: yes we can export the per-layer scale factors and activation histograms, though it's a heavy export. We'll share the top-k layers by variance.

00:07:12 Tom: would seeing weight distributions for attention layers help?

00:07:15 Sofia: absolutely, attention head weights sometimes compress poorly under int8 symmetric maps.

00:07:22 Liam: action: Sofia to produce top-layer variance report alongside per-prompt CSV.

00:07:28 Sofia: noted.

00:07:35 Liam: any red flags from legal / security regarding sharing layer-level artifacts?

00:07:40 Priya: as long as we don't get raw training data and Redwood signs the NDA addendum for debug artifacts, fine. We already have the NDA.

00:07:48 Liam: ok will flag that in the file share permissions.

00:07:55 Evan: quick note: a handful of prompts show divergent tokenization behavior between runs — likely caused by a different tokenizer version in the runtime image.

00:08:05 Devon: ah good call, I'll capture tokenizer version and exact vocab hash with the repro runs.

00:08:13 Tom: if tokenizer changes explain a chunk of regression that's actually easier to fix than quantization.

00:08:20 Priya: yes but we should assume both could be contributors; let's not conflate them.

00:08:29 Liam: moving on — fallback policies and rollouts. We recommend canary first: 5% traffic with auto rollback if user-visible regression rate > threshold for 30 minutes. For your use-case we might keep canary to internal beta only.

00:08:44 Priya: internal beta first is fine. We can't risk external user SLA.

00:08:49 Liam: ok, gating parameters: per-prompt delta threshold 0.15, cluster-level regression rate < 1.2% over 15 minutes for canary pass.

00:09:01 Anika: can Redwood add a logging hook for fallback reasons so we can audit each fallback?

00:09:06 Sofia: yes we'll attach a reason code and include prompt id, metric delta, and trace id.

00:09:12 Evan: that'll help QA triage.

00:09:18 Liam: quick breakout — any other experiments we should add?

00:09:22 Priya: maybe try asymmetric quant scales for attention layers? We heard that helps on structured tokens.

00:09:30 Sofia: we can run an int8 asymmetric sweep on just attention weights for top layers, that'll be a narrow test.

00:09:36 Tom: also test mixed-precision where the final LM head remains FP16 while other layers int8.

00:09:42 Sofia: mixed-precision head-preserve is a good mitigation often reduces hallucinations.

00:09:48 Liam: good, add both to the matrix as variants.

00:09:55 Devon: provisioning note: for repeatability we'll snapshot the instance image and seed the RNG. We'll also capture kernel/cuda/cudnn versions and tokenizer hash.

00:10:06 Anika: will Redwood share the experiment run ids and logs in the shared drive?

00:10:10 Liam: yes link will be posted to the shared sheet and I'll send a short email thread to make sure perms are right.

00:10:20 Evan: on QA, we can produce annotated diffs for the top 10 regressions with before/after spans highlighted. That will make review quicker.

00:10:30 Priya: please do that.

00:10:36 Liam: ok to recap (and this will mirror the next steps): Redwood - per-prompt csv + histograms, kv-cache disabled runs, layer variance report, provision GB16 fresh cluster; SignalCraft - blacklisted prompt set and golden labels, QA annotated diffs. Then we rerun matrix and reconvene for readout.

00:10:58 Anika: sounds good. Anything else on compliance?

00:11:03 Priya: just ensure logs are scrubbed of PII before sharing outside our secure drive. We'll mark the drive as classification "restricted".

00:11:12 Liam: noted. We'll scrub and store under restricted access.

00:11:17 Tom: one last question — how soon can we expect resolution if fallback is enabled? We need to know SLO impact.

00:11:23 Liam: fallback to FP16 will increase cost roughly 2.8x for those prompts, we'll estimate SLO impact after the top20 runs. For now assume fallback on 5% of traffic for internal beta.

00:11:36 Anika: ok thanks everyone. We'll look for the CSV and the matrix results.

00:11:44 Liam: great thanks, we'll follow up with the links and schedule the readout early next week.

00:11:50 (crosstalk)

00:11:55 Liam: end of notes — attaching references: shared sheet: https://redwood.example.com/sheets/quant-pilot-repro (internal), playbook: https://redwood.example.com/playbooks/quant-rollout (internal).

00:12:05 Transcript truncated for brevity — detailed prompt-level logs and run ids will be attached to the shared sheet.

Recap / Next steps shown above.
